item.title: State Investigating After Three Die In Custody In Same Week
item.description: “My deepest sympathies go out to the families of those who passed,” said Department of Correction Commissioner Angel Quiros. “These tragic incidents affect all those involved very deeply. I assure you that the safety and well-being of those under our supervision remains a fundamental priority.”

item.title: CT Republican Leaders Condemn State Investigation Into 2025 Police Deadly Force Incident
item.description: In a statement, three Republican leaders from the state House of Representatives, Minority Leader Vincent Candelora of North Branford, Greg Howard of Stonington and Tammy Nuccio of Tolland criticized the decision to investigate the incident. Howard is a police officer and House ranking member of the Public Safety and Security Committee. Nuccio is ranking member of the Appropriations Committee and the mother of a Connecticut state trooper.

item.title: Connecticut Lawmakers, Housing Providers Seek $123.9M To Address Rising Homelessness
item.description: The Connecticut Coalition to End Homelessness released its 2026 legislative agenda Friday, seeking roughly $123.9 million annually to expand rental assistance, prevention programs, emergency shelter capacity, and supportive housing services amid federal funding uncertainty.

item.title: CT Investigating 500-Unit Apartment Complex After Town Issues Evacuation Orders Over Conditions
item.description: Attorney General William Tong has opened an investigation into Concierge Apartments management, sending a civil investigative demand under the Connecticut Unfair Trade Practices Act seeking documentation and answers regarding the landlord’s management and response to deteriorating conditions at the Rocky Hill apartment complex.

item.description: ligible applicants can apply for reimbursement grants of up to $5,000 per year, with a maximum reimbursement of $20,000 over four years.

item.title: Lamont Once Again Extends CT’s Cold Weather Protocol
item.description: Gov. Ned Lamont for the third time has extended the state’s currently activated Severe Cold Weather protocol, this time until noon on Feb. 15.

item.title: Investigation Finds Lack Of Oversight When Disabled Students Sent Out Of State
item.description: A lack of oversight, unexplained injuries, and practices inconsistent with state law were issues highlighted in a report released Tuesday as the result of a multi-year investigation into the widespread out-of-state placement of Connecticut students with disabilities.

item.title: CT Municipal Leaders Call For Education Funding Changes As State Support Lags Behind Inflation
item.description: In Seymour, First Selectwoman Annmarie Drugonis said education represented 65% of the town’s budget.

item.title: CT Senate Republicans Roll Out Affordability Plan That Cuts Taxes On Families Earning Under $200K
item.description: State Sen. Ryan Fazio, R-Greenwich, said the state could make up for the resulting revenue shortfall in the short term through adjustments to the state’s volatility cap, which is a limit on so-called volatile tax revenue, primarily personal income and pass-through taxes.
